title: Where Does 2 m of DNA Fit? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
In biology class, the teacher said one human cell holds about two metres of DNA. Diya asks: cells are too small to see, so where does two metres of thread fit? The answer is the nucleus, the control room of the cell, where the thread is packed into chromosomes.

You will meet Robert Brown (1831) and Flemming, see what chromatin is made of, then a zoom ladder from a cell to the nucleus (chromatin, nuclear matrix, nucleolus), the nuclear envelope with its perinuclear space and a nuclear pore. Watch chromatin coil and fold into chromosomes, then the 46 chromosomes of a human cell. Then the centromere, kinetochores and satellite, the four types by centromere position, chromatin vs chromosomes side by side, a pause and think, four chromosomes named, the no-nucleus exam trap, an original NEET-pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 67 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
